blocks.text: When Mordecai refuses to bow before Haman, the newly promoted Persian official responds not with personal vengeance but with a plot of massive scale. Learning that Mordecai is Jewish, Haman resolves to destroy not merely one man but an entire ethnic and religious community throughout the Persian kingdom.

Haman presents his case to King Ahasuerus by characterizing the Jewish people as a dispersed population whose diverse laws make them a liability to the empire's unity and the king's authority. He offers to finance their destruction from the royal treasury, securing the king's seal and authorization for his edict.

Haman casts the pur—the lot—to determine the date of execution. The lot falls on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, establishing a distant but inevitable deadline for the genocide he has engineered against all Jews throughout Ahasuerus's realm.
